subject.title: fix(agent-core): bound harness exec stdout/stderr at 16 MiB

question: Should `NodeExecutionEnv.exec` truncate captured stdout and stderr at 16 MiB per stream by default, with `maxOutputBytes` as the supported opt-up path for callers that intentionally need larger captures?
rationale: The patch fixes a real availability risk, but it changes the exported agent-core shell execution return contract for existing large-output consumers; automation should not choose that compatibility tradeoff by itself.

options.title: Accept bounded capture as the new contract
options.body: Land this PR with the 16 MiB per-stream default and treat `maxOutputBytes` as the supported opt-up for intentionally large returned output.

options.title: Require explicit compatibility proof
options.body: Ask for focused evidence that current harness consumers needing full large captures can safely raise `maxOutputBytes` before accepting the default cap.

options.title: Preserve full capture by default
options.body: Pause this branch and redesign around an opt-in cap if maintainers consider unbounded full capture part of the current harness contract.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded capture as the new contract
recommendation.body: Land this PR with the 16 MiB per-stream default and treat `maxOutputBytes` as the supported opt-up for intentionally large returned output.

likelyOwner.reason: The agent-core extraction and adjacent process-output hardening history make this the clearest available owner for the compatibility contract decision.
